picks.title: Treasury Department proposes curbs on high-tech investments, including AI, in China, Russia, North Korea
picks.rationale: Geopolitics and policy axis. An official proposed rule: Treasury would expand the Outbound Investment Security Program to cover U.S. investments over $50,000 in AI and other critical tech in countries of concern, implementing the 2025 COINS Act. This directly changes where U.S. AI capital can go. Lead with the rule text and avoid characterising motives.
picks.excerpt: Treasury proposed a rule expanding the Outbound Investment Security Program to cover US investments over $50,000 in AI, HPC, quantum, hypersonics and biotech in China, Russia, North Korea and other countries of concern, implementing the 2025 COINS Act.

picks.title: Chancellor unveils Britain's ambitious plan for AI
picks.rationale: Policy axis, primary document. HM Treasury announced a national AI package covering adoption across the UK, scaling domestic AI firms and security against AI threats. It is a new government release, separate from the 10-15 defence card and the 10-20 sovereignty paper. Describe the measures as announced; 'ambitious' is the government's word and should be attributed to it.
picks.excerpt: Major package to unlock the opportunities of AI in every postcode, scale up home grown AI firms, and keep UK safe from threats announced by the Chancellor.

picks.title: Opposition deepfake video of Spanish PM's wife sparks outrage before election
picks.rationale: Elections axis. A party-produced AI video showing synthetic likenesses of people linked to Spain's governing party appearing to admit wrongdoing, released before the election. The story exists only because of the AI video. Neutrality: describe the video and attribute the reactions to named parties; take no side.
picks.excerpt: Video shows AI likenesses of people linked to Pedro Sánchez’s Socialist party appearing to admit to wrongdoing

picks.title: Texas becomes the latest state to sue OpenAI
picks.rationale: Policy and litigation axis. A follow-up with a new filing: the Texas Attorney General filed a separate suit against OpenAI and Sam Altman over ChatGPT safety. Texas was not one of the eight states in the 10-15 card, and its suit names Altman personally. The harms are allegations and must be attributed to Paxton.
picks.excerpt: Similar to the lawsuits filed by Arizona, West Virginia, Iowa, and several others, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton accuses OpenAI of misleading users about the safety of ChatGPT, allegedly exposing children and other users to a “litany of harms” that’s “driven by the company’s insatiable quest to win the AI arms race and amass large fortunes.”

picks.title: DeepSeek and MiniMax cleared to take AI models abroad, state media says
picks.rationale: Geopolitics axis. A follow-up with a new decision: under China's proposed AI export controls, the commerce ministry has completed export registrations for DeepSeek and MiniMax to release models open-source and license them overseas. These are the first clearances under the regime. Attribute the clearance to state media and MiniMax's statement.
picks.excerpt: Under China AI export controls, “AI companies can continue with their commercialization efforts as usual,” a CCTV-linked account says.

https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i.new_action: New filing: Texas AG Ken Paxton filed his own lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman. Texas was not among the eight states in the 10-15 card.
